title: httpfs support for HTTP[S] proxy and custom SSL cert bundle
body:
### What happens?

_As suggested, moved from #5944_ 

I'm currently trying to use DuckDB in a corporate environment where our AWS access goes via an HTTP[s] proxy.
This means the proxy intercepts the HTTPS traffic and requires that we use a custom SSL certificate bundle.
In the case of tools such boto, it requires us setting the `AWS_CA_BUNDLE`.

There doesn't appear to be a way to configure the httpfs to support a custom CA bundle and I think it also might not honor the `HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY` and `no_proxy` environment variables.

I will attach a notebook that demonstrates the error I see, which is:
```
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
Error                                     Traceback (most recent call last)
Cell In[7], line 1
----> 1 result = con.execute("select * from 's3://fiaim-all-trp-dev-shared/portfolio/AIALPHAGGB|9888/2018-05-18/results.parquet'")

Error: Invalid Error: HTTP HEAD error on '[https://s3.amazonaws.com/fiaim-all-trp-dev-shared/portfolio/AIALPHAGGB|9888/2018-05-18/results.parquet](https://s3.amazonaws.com/fiaim-all-trp-dev-shared/portfolio/AIALPHAGGB%7C9888/2018-05-18/results.parquet)' (Error code 8)
```

### To Reproduce

- Install httpfs
- Behind a corporate firewall:
  - execute a `con.execute(f"select * from 's3://{bucket}/{key}'")`

### OS:

x64

### DuckDB Version:

0.6.1

### DuckDB Client:

Python

### Full Name:

Dan Oxlade

### Affiliation:

N/A

### Have you tried this on the latest `master` branch?

- [X] I agree

- [X] I agree

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Hi DuckDB team, hi all,

First and foremost, thanks for sharing such a great and inspiring program, wow! :)

In deploying a private PKI with its own root and intermediate CAs, I've been exploring how DuckDB + httpfs behave when grabbing data from a private MinIO instance over TLS using a certificate issued by the private CA.

In my preliminary testing it seems that duckdb 0.9.2 does not validate MinIO's server certificate.

My basic test is a query like:
```
INSTALL httpfs;
LOAD httpfs;

SET s3_endpoint='s3.....local';
SET s3_access_key_id='...';
SET s3_secret_access_key='...';
SET s3_use_ssl=true;
SET s3_region='';
SET s3_url_style='path';

SELECT count(1) as count
FROM parquet_scan('s3://bucket/dataset/**/*.parquet');
```

My test environments:

* macOS with the Root CA certificate imported and trusted into KeyChain.
* CentOS 7 servers with the Root CA certificate trusted by the system's OpenSSL.
* Debian 12 Container not trusting the private Root CA.

On the three systems I tested:

* duckdb CLI -- works nicely.
* Python duckdb -- works nicely.

Then, on macOS, I also tested DBeaver via duckdb_jdbc.jar -- worked nicely.

Outstanding in my tests:

* Windows trusting the Root CA -- CLI and Python.
* Java programs on CentOS 7 trusting the Root CA.

However, so far, by the experiment with the Debian 12 container, it does seem that duckdb (or the httpfs extension?) do not validate the HTTP server's certificate against a list of trusted roots.

Can anyone confirm similar observations?
Thanks in advance!

comments.body:
Okay so [polars](https://docs.pola.rs/) to the rescue! The use of proxy environment variables is implemented within this package it would seem. So for those behind a proxy, here's a low-effort work-around that you can try that still keeps duckdb in the mix in case you want to be able to switch back later and remove the polars dependency when someone cleverer than me implements the proxy fix in duckdb.

Credit to @participant15 for coming up with this hack.

Assuming you have your `http_proxy` and `https_proxy` environment variables set and replace the _XXXXX_ values ...

```python
import polars as pl
import duckdb

source = "s3://XXXXX/*.parquet"

storage_options = {
    "aws_access_key_id": "XXXXX",
    "aws_secret_access_key": "XXXXX",
    "aws_session_token": "XXXXX",
    "aws_region": "XXXXX"
}

polars_scan = pl.scan_parquet(source, storage_options=storage_options).lazy()

con = duckdb.connect(':<nick>:')

df = con.execute("SELECT * FROM polars_scan;").df()

print(df)
```

May also be of interest to those watching #3836 and #4741
